_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH. Edit here, then run: python3 build.py. That regenerates the PDF and rewrites the app's data block. Never edit the exercise tables in the PDF or the app by hand.
_app_name_warning: app.name is the key the tracker uses to prefill last session's load. Renaming it orphans that exercise's history. Change app.name only if you mean to reset it.

meta.title: Building Back
meta.subtitle:
A 24-week sustainable strength program
for a recurrent L5/S1 disc herniation
meta.starting_point: ~6 weeks post June 2026 flare, improving but symptomatic

1.title: Re-entry
1.heading: Phase 1 — Re-entry (weeks 1–4)
1.goal_pdf: establish a symptom-free baseline, rebuild trunk endurance and hip strength, and prove to your nervous system that loading is safe. You are not trying to get stronger in these four weeks. You are collecting evidence about what your back tolerates.
1.rules_pdf: Rules for this phase. Everything at RPE 5–6. No hip hinge under external load — the hinge pattern is trained through back extensions and pull-throughs, which give you the posterior chain without the lever arm. Controlled tempo: 2 seconds down, no bounce. If you finish a session thinking “that was easy,” the phase is working as intended.
1.goal_app: Establish a symptom-free baseline and rebuild trunk endurance. You are not trying to get stronger — you are collecting evidence about what your back tolerates.
rules_app: Everything at RPE 5-6, four or more reps left in the tank.
No hip hinge under external load yet.
If it feels easy, the phase is working.
1.footer_pdf:
Passing out of Phase 1
Move to Phase 2 when you have completed four consecutive weeks with no Red days and you finish sessions feeling the same or better than when you started. If week 4 has been anything other than clean, repeat weeks 3–4. Repeating a phase costs you two weeks; a fourth herniation costs you six months.

2.title: Build
2.heading: Phase 2 — Build (weeks 5–12)
2.goal_pdf: this is where the muscle gets built. Loads climb into a genuinely productive range, the hip hinge is reintroduced under load, and volume increases. RPE 6–8. Reps 6–12.
2.rules_pdf: What changes. The trap bar deadlift enters — from elevated blocks or the high handles, never from the floor in this phase. The elevated start position keeps your torso more upright and cuts the shear demand on your lumbar spine while still loading the hips and posterior chain hard. Dumbbell RDLs appear with a deliberately short range. Everything else gets heavier.
2.goal_app: Where the muscle gets built. Loads climb into a productive range and the hip hinge returns under load.
rules_app: Trap bar from blocks or high handles only — never the floor.
Only progress a lift if last week was green.
2.footer_pdf:
Passing out of Phase 2
Move to Phase 3 when you have completed eight weeks with no more than two Amber days and zero Red days, your trap bar has climbed meaningfully, and your single-leg calf raise benchmark (Section 7) is within 20% side to side.

3.title: Strength
3.heading: Phase 3 — Strength (weeks 13–24)
3.goal_pdf: consolidate. Lower reps, heavier loads, more demanding variations — but the same spine-sparing exercise selection. This is the phase you can stay in indefinitely.
3.rules_pdf: What changes. Main lifts drop to 4–6 reps at RPE 7–8. Loaded rotation is introduced, carefully, through cable chops. The trap bar may come down toward the floor only if the previous eight weeks were entirely Green and you can maintain a neutral spine at that start position — check this with your physio, and film a set from the side. There is no requirement to ever pull from the floor.
3.goal_app: Consolidate. Heavier loads, same spine-sparing exercise selection. You can stay in this phase indefinitely.
rules_app: Loaded rotation introduced carefully via cable chops.
Floor pulls only after 8 fully green weeks, and only with your physio's sign-off.
There is no requirement to ever pull from the floor.

home_routine.name: Sciatic nerve slide
home_routine.cue: Sit tall, slump slightly. Straighten the knee while you look up; bend the knee while you look down. Slow and smooth. This should feel like gentle traffic through the leg, never like a stretch or a symptom. Back off immediately if it does.

app.cue: Straighten the knee while looking up, bend it while looking down. Gentle traffic, never a stretch or a symptom.

home_routine.name: Prone press-up
home_routine.cue: Lie face down, press your upper body up on your hands, hips stay down. Hold 2s. Only if extension makes you feel better — most L5/S1 disc presentations respond to extension, but test it. If it worsens symptoms, replace with 90/90 breathing.

app.cue: Only if extension makes you feel better. If it worsens things, do 90/90 breathing instead.

home_routine.name: 90/90 diaphragmatic breathing
home_routine.cue: On your back, feet on a wall or chair, knees at 90°. Breathe into your belly and low ribs, long slow exhale. Resets a guarded, over-braced trunk.

app.name: 90/90 breathing
app.cue: Feet up, knees at 90. Breathe into belly and low ribs. Resets an over-braced trunk.

home_routine.name: Glute bridge
home_routine.cue: Ribs down, squeeze at the top, 2s hold.

home_routine.name: Dead bug
home_routine.cue: You already do this. Keep the low back flat against the floor — that is the whole exercise.

app.cue: Low back stays flat against the floor. That is the whole exercise.

home_routine.name: Bird dog
home_routine.cue: You already do this. Draw a small square with the extended hand and foot for a progression.

app.cue: Draw a small square with the extended hand and foot to progress.

home_routine.name: Side plank
home_routine.cue: Completes the McGill “big three”. Knees bent version is fine.

app.cue: Knees bent version is fine.

home_routine.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
home_routine.cue: Tuck the pelvis first, then lean. Tight hip flexors make your lumbar spine compensate all day.

app.cue: Tuck the pelvis first, then lean.

nerve_work.name: Single-leg stand
nerve_work.cue: Progress: eyes open on the floor → eyes closed on the floor → eyes open on a cushion → eyes closed on a cushion.

app.cue: Progress: eyes open, then eyes closed, then on a cushion.

nerve_work.name: Heel walks and toe walks
nerve_work.cue: Simple, and directly tests the L5 and S1 myotomes.

app.name: Heel and toe walks
app.cue: Directly tests the L5 and S1 myotomes.

Loads the legs hard without axial compression through the spine.
Removes the need for your spine to resist the load at all.

Less hip-flexor stretch, less pelvic tilt demand.

changelog.note: Cable lateral raise added to Day A and Day C in all three phases. The program had no direct medial deltoid work; presses cover the anterior head and face pulls the posterior head. Placed on the two shortest/least shoulder-loaded days, and folded into the Day C cable superset as a tri-set, so total added session time is roughly five minutes a week.

Cable lateral raise removed from Day A in all three phases; Day A was running well over its estimated time, and the raise was the only exercise there not serving the squat, hinge or trunk brief. It stays on Day C, where it is tri-set into the existing cable station and costs no extra time. Phase 1 Day C raised from 2 to 3 sets to partly offset the lost volume; Phases 2 and 3 stay at 3 sets. Side-delt frequency drops from twice to once a week, which is an acceptable trade for a single-joint isolation movement.

Every exercise tagged with a muscle group and a spinal-load class. Flare protocol rewritten as a five-stage return ladder that the phone app now applies automatically to the session it shows you. App gains a full session history with loads, editing, and a progression chart by muscle group.

Pain is now logged as a 0-10 score on both the gym session and the daily check-in, which is what goes to the physio. The traffic light is derived from that number plus the below-the-knee toggle, so the flare ladder and the phase rules are unchanged.

_groups_comment: group = primary muscle group used by the app's progression chart. spine = spinal load class (1 low, 2 moderate, 3 high) used by the flare protocol to decide which exercises are allowed at each return stage. Both are consumed by build.py.

flare_protocol._comment: Drives both Section 8 of the PDF and the app's adaptive flare mode. clear_days is counted from the most recent setback (flare start, any red session or check-in, or any session logged with symptoms below the knee). max_spine filters exercises by their 'spine' tag; pool_phase 0 means use the phase you are currently in.
flare_protocol.intro: You will have a flare at some point in 24 weeks. Having a written plan for it is the difference between losing a week and losing a season - and it stops you making the panic decision to stop moving entirely, which reliably makes things worse.
flare_protocol.clear_day_rule: A clear day is a day with no Red logged and no symptoms below the knee. Any Red session, Red morning check-in, or session logged with leg symptoms resets the count to zero and drops you back to the stage that count belongs to.

stages.title: Settle
stages.summary: No gym. Walking, reduced-range home routine, nerve slides.
do: Do not go to bed. Bed rest beyond a day makes disc-related pain worse, not better.
Walk short and often - 5-10 minutes every couple of hours beats one long walk.
Find your position of relief and use it: prone, prone on elbows, or standing.
Nerve slides gently, 2 x 10 per leg, twice a day. Reduce range until there is no provocation at all.
Avoid prolonged sitting entirely. Stand or lie down.
Contact your physio now. Do not wait to see whether it settles on its own.

stages.title: Reintroduce
stages.summary: Back in the gym, spine-neutral work only, half your pre-flare loads.
do: Supported and machine work only - nothing that loads the spine through range.
Two working sets, never more. You should leave feeling you could have done twice as much.
Home routine daily at full range again, walks toward 20-30 minutes.
Any leg symptom during or within 24h of a session sends you back to Settle.

stages.title: Rebuild
stages.summary: Phase 1 as written minus the hinge, at 70% of pre-flare loads.
do: Squat pattern, carries and rows return. The loaded hinge does not.
Run this for at least a week even if everything feels fine.
Re-test the single-leg calf raise and compare it to your last benchmark.

stages.title: Re-load
stages.summary: Your normal phase, hinge still held back, 85% of pre-flare loads.
do: Back to the phase you were in, with the heavy hinge and loaded rotation still parked.
Sets as written. Loads are the brake here, not volume.
Write the debrief now if you have not already.

stages.title: Full programme
stages.summary: Everything back, 95% of pre-flare loads. One clear week from closing the flare.
do: The hinge returns at the lightest load you would call productive, and climbs from there.
Do not chase the number you were at before the flare. It will come back faster than you think.
After a clear week here the flare is closed and you are back on the normal progression.

flare_protocol.debrief: Within a week of any flare, write down: what you did in the 72 hours before it; whether the gym or daily life was the more likely cause; and what specifically you will change. Three episodes without a written debrief means the pattern that caused them is still invisible to you. This takes ten minutes and is probably the highest-leverage thing in this entire document.

spine_labels.1: Low - supported or machine, no spinal loading through range
spine_labels.2: Moderate - upright loading, controlled, no hinge under load
spine_labels.3: High - loaded hinge, axial squat, loaded rotation

pain_scale._comment: Single source for the 0-10 pain score. The app logs the number plus the below-the-knee toggle and derives the traffic light from these bands, so the flare ladder, the deload trigger and the phase-progression rule all keep working while the number is what goes to the physio. leg_symptoms_forces means any symptom below the knee is Red regardless of the number.
pain_scale.prompt: Worst back pain since the last log

bands.criteria: No leg symptoms. Back stiffness or ache at or below 3/10 that settles within 24 hours.
bands.action: Train as written. Progress as written. This is where the programme is designed to run.

bands.criteria: Back pain 4-6/10, or stiffness that lingers more than 24 hours, but no symptoms below the knee.
bands.action: Train, but: hold your loads where they are (do not add weight), cut the number of working sets by roughly a third, drop the hinge pattern for that session, and keep everything at RPE 5. Do not skip the session - movement helps here, load progression does not. Return to Green rules once you have had two consecutive Green days.
bands.action_app: Hold your loads, cut sets by a third, drop the hinge, everything at RPE 5. Do not skip the session.

bands.criteria: Any pain, numbness, tingling or heaviness below the knee, whatever the number. Any new weakness. Symptoms spreading further down the leg than yesterday. Or back pain at 7/10 or above.
bands.action: Stop loading. Walking, the daily home routine at reduced range, and nerve slides only. Contact your physio. The app opens a flare for you and rebuilds your sessions from stage 0 upward - see Section 8.
bands.action_app: Stop loading. Walking, home routine at reduced range, nerve slides. Contact your physio.

pain_scale.note: Symptoms moving toward your back are good news even if the number is unchanged. Symptoms moving down the leg mean stop, however mild and whatever the number says.
